4k at 60fps is a pretty empty promise. It's the kind of thing that sounds great until you realize that it'll be literally years before the average streamer is capable of broadcasting at that resolution/framerate, and about as long before broadband internet can reliably stream at that rate.

Don't get me wrong, it's a step in the right direction, but when you consider the kind of hardware you need right now just to be able to play a game at 4k/60fps and then stop and think about the further demands placed on that hardware to package the data for streaming... Twin Titans with a 6 core processor and 32+ GB of RAM is what I would expect to see handling that kind of task.

What it comes down to is a Twitch competitor throwing out trendy jargon to draw in people who don't know any better. HTML5 is great, and Twitch could add it at any time. It's a selling feature but the bigger selling feature is what kind of content you can find on the platform. If your favorite streamers aren't on Hitbox, they aren't exactly providing a huge amount of legit reason to make the switch.
4k 60fps doesn't apply to just 3D games, you could easily stream something like Ori and the Blind Forest at that resolution and framerate if you don't have Australian or US internet
With my gigabit I see no problem with 4K at 60fps. Problem is the lack of platforms and content.

It's not just a question of whether or not you can get the game to run at 60fps with 4k resolution. You also have to be able to package that data and upload it, and then people have to be able to stream it fast enough to make it worthwhile. There are too many links in the chain that current hardware/bandwidth can't maintain.
Plus, Hitbox doesn't censor games just yet.
